title: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 Requires 567MB of RAM for On-Device Multimodal AI

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Google has detailed the operational requirements for its open-weights multimodal AI model in a technical report released this week. The document outlines that the 744M parameter EmbeddingGemma 2 requires 567MB of active RAM to run the full model with 4-bit weights on a Pixel 11 Pro, while a text-only version uses 191MB. The model's context window has increased fourfold to 8K tokens, allowing a single input to contain up to 58 video frames or 5.5 minutes of audio, and is distributed under an Apache 2.0 license for on-device search and retrieval.

The model was built using Gemma 4 as a base and trained to mimic the performance of Gemini Embedding 2 via contrastive training. Technical benchmarks show that direct speech embedding scored 69.54 on the MSEB spoken-query retrieval benchmark, surpassing the 57.59 score achieved by transcribing audio first. For code search, the new model scored 78.68 on MTEB Code, an increase over the 68.76 posted by EmbeddingGemma 1.

selectedTweets.text:
Banger report from Google.

They just released EmbeddingGemma 2, an open 744M multimodal embedding model.

It beats specialist models and models 2 to 12 times larger across seven benchmark suites covering text, code, images, video, documents, and audio.

Text, images, audio, video, and mixed inputs all go into one vector space. Each modality has its own encoder feeding into a shared backbone, so you can load only what you need. Text-only runs at 271M parameters, vision-language at 439M, and audio-language at 577M.

It scores 61.36 on MTEB Multilingual v2 and 68.46 on MTEB English v2. The int4 version loses about 0.4 points on MTEB Multilingual.

You can also lower the vision token budget and truncate the embedding dimensions.

For agent memory and retrieval over mixed media, this small open model is a great on-device option.

selectedTweets.text:
Google released its EmbeddingGemma 2 paper. 

embedding model for on-device multimodal AI, under an Apache 2.0 license.

> puts text, code, images, audio and video into 1 searchable space on phones. gives phones a missing piece: a way to understand and search your own stuff without sending it to a server.

> shows that a 744M-parameter open model can embed text, images, audio, and video, beating many models 2 to 12 times larger.

> On a Pixel 11 Pro, quantized text weights take about 191MB of active RAM, and the full multimodal model takes about 567MB.

> The context window grows 4x to 8K tokens, enough for roughly 5.5 minutes of audio, 29 images or 58 video frames in 1 input.

They built EmbeddingGemma 2 on Gemma 4, trained it to copy the larger Gemini Embedding 2, then tuned it with contrastive training. All media types share 1 vector space, and the full model fits in 567 MB on a Pixel 11 Pro with 4-bit weights.

Embedding speech directly beat transcribing it, 69.54 versus 57.59 on the MSEB spoken-query retrieval benchmark. Code search scored 78.68 on MTEB Code, up from 68.76 for EmbeddingGemma 1.
